name: Numerical Methods
strandNote: All roles: every pricer, fit and backtest is a numerical method.
description: Know when a computed number is accurate, and price one option three numerical ways.

lessonNames.l1-floating-point: How a computer stores a number
lessonNames.l6-safe-root-finder: A root finder that never fails
lessonNames.l13-finite-differences: Finite differences for a pricing equation

lessonObjectives.l1-floating-point: Read a double’s sign, exponent and mantissa, and find machine epsilon.
lessonObjectives.l2-cancellation: Spot catastrophic cancellation and rewrite a formula to avoid it.
lessonObjectives.l3-conditioning: Compute a condition number and predict how much input error is amplified.
lessonObjectives.l4-stability: Compare normal equations with QR for least squares and explain which is stable.
lessonObjectives.l5-bisection-and-newton: Compare the convergence rates of bisection, secant and Newton’s method.
lessonObjectives.l6-safe-root-finder: Build a safeguarded Newton method and use it for implied volatility on every strike.
lessonObjectives.l7-interpolation: Fit an interpolating polynomial and see Runge’s wiggles at the ends.
lessonObjectives.l8-splines: Fit a cubic spline through yields and read off rates between the quoted points.
lessonObjectives.l9-quadrature: Integrate with the trapezium and Simpson rules and measure their error order.
lessonObjectives.l10-gaussian-quadrature: Price a European option by Gauss-Legendre quadrature against the lognormal density.
lessonObjectives.l11-step-size: Measure a solver’s error order from a log-log plot, and choose a step for a tolerance.
lessonObjectives.l12-stiff-equations: See an explicit solver blow up on a stiff equation, and fix it with an implicit step.
lessonObjectives.l13-finite-differences: Replace derivatives with differences on a grid and solve the Black-Scholes equation explicitly.
lessonObjectives.l14-implicit-and-crank-nicolson: Compare the stability and error of explicit, implicit and Crank-Nicolson schemes.
lessonObjectives.l15-monte-carlo-error: Estimate a Monte Carlo price with its standard error, and see the $1/\sqrt{n}$ rate.
lessonObjectives.l16-control-variates: Cut Monte Carlo error with antithetic draws and a control variate.
lessonObjectives.l17-three-ways: Price one European option by finite differences, quadrature and Monte Carlo, and explain each error.
